newsitem.title: INDIA: CARE downgrades Western India Shipyard debenture.
newsitem.headline: CARE downgrades Western India Shipyard debenture.

text.p: The Credit Analysis and Research Ltd (CARE) said on Tuesday it downgraded the rating of the partly convertible debenture (PCD) issue of 707 million rupees of Western India Shipyard Ltd (WISL) to "CARE D" from "CARE BBB+ Triple B plus.

"The PCD has a non-convertible portion of 424 million rupees. Instruments with CARE D rating are of the lowest category. They are either in default or are likely to be in default soon," CARE said in a statement.
WISL had issued the PCDs to part finance two new projects; a ship repair yard and a ship breaking yard.

The projects have suffered time and cost overruns. The ship repair yard began operations in January 1996, with a delay of six months, while the ship breaking yard has not yet commenced operations, CARE said.
With cost overrun and inadequate working capital facilities, the company is facing a serious liquidity crunch, leading to a default in interest payment to PCD holders, CARE said.
A review by the financial institutions is on hand and a decision regarding financing of cost overrun is expected shortly, it said.
